ops.title: ccx's push-rejection classifiers verified against real git 2.51 and jj 0.43 — all five arms live
ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-03 by building real bare-origin/two-clone setups in /tmp and
capturing verbatim stdout+stderr. Every substring `internal/cli/shippush.go`
classifies on appears in real output, **on stderr, at exit 1**, on both tools:

| substring | site | tool |
|---|---|---|
| `(non-fast-forward)` | `:41` gitPushRejected | git |
| `(fetch first)` | `:41` gitPushRejected | git |
| `(stale info)` | `:47` gitPushStaleLease | git |
| `[remote rejected]` | `:38` veto | git |
| `unexpectedly moved on the remote` | `:19`/`:56` jjPushRejected | jj |

No stream mismatch of the kind the gt conflict banner hit (that one printed to
stdout where a classifier read stderr). Zero dead arms.

**`(non-fast-forward)` and `(fetch first)` are distinct conditions, and matching
both is necessary.** It took two different setups to produce them: git says
non-fast-forward once the remote-tracking ref has been fetched, and fetch-first
when it has not. That maps onto ship's flow exactly — `shipPushGitOnce` fetches
first, so its own rejection is non-FF, while a concurrent push landing *between*
ship's fetch and its push yields fetch-first. Both are reachable from real
timing.

**Why both tools say "stale info":** jj pushes with an expected-old-value
(force-with-lease semantics), so when the remote moved, git's ref-rejection
reason code is `stale info` and jj surfaces that reason verbatim.
`gitPushStaleLease` and `jjPushRejected` classify the SAME underlying git
condition through two tool surfaces — which is why the token is shared and why
keeping the two arms separate is correct.

**The near-miss worth remembering.** jj prints `refs/heads/main (reason: stale
info)`. `gitPushStaleLease` requires the literal `(stale info)` — `(` immediately
before `stale` — so jj's text does NOT satisfy it today. If jj ever reworded to
`refs/heads/main (stale info)`, a jj push failure would start satisfying git's
stale-lease classifier as well. Verified mechanically, not by eye. Also
confirmed jj's stderr contains none of git's human-form tokens.

**Two claims still untested**, named rather than implied: (1) the
`[remote rejected]` veto exists for a multi-ref push mixing a non-FF ref with a
hook-declined ref — a single-ref decline produces `[remote rejected]` with no
`(non-fast-forward)` anywhere, so the veto never had to fire; (2) `:55-56`
requires jjPushRejected never match jj's bare `Failed to push some bookmarks`,
"which a permission failure also prints" — unconfirmed, needs an auth-rejecting
remote.

These strings are version-pinned to jj 0.43 and git's per-ref reason tokens. The
value of a real-fixture test here is durability, not a bug fix: it regenerates
the bytes every run instead of freezing 2026 wording into a shell heredoc.
